objective: Bounded single-H800 environment probe: establish device allocation, record sanitized runtime/driver/GPU metadata, run a small MuJoCo CPU reference contact scene and the matching MJWarp GPU scene (1 and 32 worlds), and check finite states, contact behavior and selected CPU/GPU tolerances inside one Slurm job (max 1 GPU, 4 CPUs, 20-minute wall time).

config.scene: single actuated capsule fingertip (slide joint, position actuator kp=20) pressing a static box trackpad; timestep 1/240 s; 480 steps
config.device: NVIDIA H800 (81559 MiB, sm_90), driver 580.173.02, CUDA driver version 13.0

allocation_lifecycle.job_identity: raw scheduler job id held in ignored private receipt (.local/private-receipt.json); public correlation hash sha256(job_id)[:12] = 435b4de29fe9

performance_methodology: Warmup = wall time of the first mjw.step after put_data per batch configuration (dominated by one-time Warp kernel compilation, 25.3 s on first config, ~0.005 s once cached). Steady state = 480 consecutive mjw.step calls on a fresh batch, wall-timed between warp device synchronizations. Numbers are measured on this 1-DOF probe scene only; no extrapolation to larger scenes, world counts, or full-hand throughput is made. CPU reference throughput is reported for the same tiny scene and is not a GPU claim.

artifacts.path: probe raw output JSON (kept in ignored private storage; identical content on the cluster workdir)

failures: First probe submission failed within 4 s: probe script used warp get_device(int), which warp-lang 1.18.0 rejects ('Invalid device identifier: 0'). Fixed to get_cuda_device(0) plus an explicit ScopedDevice('cuda:0'); CPU-only smoke re-passed; second submission completed. This was a probe-script bug, not a scheduler, driver, or MJWarp solver failure. The failed attempt's allocation was released automatically by job exit.
limitations: Environment validation only: no rendering, no Allegro/hand model, no GUI, no policy or training code exercised.
Tiny 1-DOF contact scene at 1/32 worlds; throughput numbers describe this scene only and make no full-hand or large-batch claim.

GPU aggregate throughput at both 1 and 32 worlds remained below the single-world CPU reference in this tiny scene. Batching increased GPU aggregate throughput, but no GPU-over-CPU crossover was measured. This ungraphed stepping loop is not an optimized full-hand benchmark.
CPU/GPU trajectory agreement (~4e-9 m) reflects this deterministic settle scene; tolerance choices for future richer scenes remain open.
Warp kernel compilation (25.3 s one-time, cached under the cluster home) must be budgeted into any short GPU job.
Rendering/Allegro/GUI/policy training remain unverified and out of scope.
